data.narrative:
Helion Energy, a Series G nuclear energy company founded by David Kirtley and Chris Pihl, is evaluated against a peer universe of 11 comparable companies spanning public markets (3 firms including Oklo, Nano Nuclear Energy, and others trading on OKLO, NNE, SMR) and private capital (8 firms including Valar Atomics and Fuse Energy). The company has raised $1.5B+ to date against a stated valuation of $15.5B.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the last post-money value of $5.4B and applying a 1.25x multiplier typical for Series G advancement, implies $6.8B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, similar-valuation-tier comparables—Oklo ($7.0B), Valar Atomics ($6.0B), and X-Energy ($5.6B)—yields a median of $6.0B, establishing a range of $5.6B to $7.0B. Triangulation across both methods produces a low of $5.1B, median of $6.4B, and high of $7.8B.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5.1B to $7.8B, with a central estimate near $6.4B. The current stated valuation of $15.5B sits substantially above this range. Key uncertainties include capital-efficiency trajectory relative to peers, technology-development risk, and regulatory pathway clarity—factors not fully captured in comparable multiples alone.
